gateway: isolated temporary home, approval=reads; a freshly seeded gateway for the stub screenshots, one for the live ones and one for the walkthrough
data: fictional, seeded through the app's HTTP API (capture/scenes.json)

agent_backend.live_model: the operator's own installed, signed-in kiro-cli over ACP with model "auto"; the replies on screen are that model's and vary from run to run
agent_backend.stub: Kiro Crew's offline stub ACP backend (capture/stub_backend.py) for every other scene; no chat reply is shown from it
agent_backend.credit_reading: the browser answers the top bar's credit readout (/api/sessions/usage) with "no reading", so no account balance or email can be shown

note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: capture.py's setup installed it from this checkout (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, and every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and backend. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in issue-radar and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is main at the pinned commit with only the built-in's registration removed (its BUILTIN_NAMES row and its package directory); kirocrew_tree_dirty records that. The gateway's `gh` was this repository's capture/fake_gh/gh (KIROCREW_GH_BIN, and first on PATH for the agent's shell), which answers from the fictional repository in capture/fake_gh/repo.json: no real repository, account or network was used.
data_notes: The repository example-outfitters/trail-planner, its issues, pull requests, comments, labels, checks and every login (all ending in -example) are made up for this README and served by capture/fake_gh/gh; avatars are empty.
The repository was connected through the app's own POST /connect (capture/scenes.json setup).
The AI summaries and suggested labels were written by the live model during the capture; the investigation chat is a live agent session that read the issue through the fake gh after one approval.
Relative times ("2 days ago") are against the fixture's fixed dates and the gateway's clock during the capture.
Links to the fictional repository point at github.com, because that is the host the app is built for; the owner example-outfitters is made up and nothing was fetched from it.
